title: NY State Assembly · District 70

context.text: Incumbent Jordan Wright defeated Conrad Blackburn 53.9% to 45.7% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. Blackburn had also won the Working Families Party primary and would have appeared on the WFP line in the general election, but as of this guide's research Ballotpedia lists him among 'withdrawn or disqualified' candidates for the November general election, leaving Wright unopposed on the ballot. The Republican primary was canceled with no candidate.

summary.text: Jordan Wright has represented Assembly District 70 in Central Harlem since January 2025. He previously served as chief of staff to City Council Member Yusef Salaam and is the son of former Assembly Member Keith L.T. Wright. He defeated a primary challenge from Conrad Blackburn and is unopposed in the general election.

background.text: Wright was born and raised in New York City and is a lifelong resident of Central Harlem. He graduated from Syracuse University in 2017 with a degree in psychology.
After college he worked as an educator in multiple Manhattan schools before serving for a number of years on his local community board.
He most recently served as Chief of Staff to New York City Council Member Yusef Salaam before resigning to take his Assembly seat in January 2025.
He is the son of former Assembly Member Keith L.T. Wright and the grandson of former New York State Supreme Court Judge Bruce Wright.

In the 2025-2026 session he serves on the Aging, Banks, Economic Development/Job Creation/Commerce and Industry, Libraries and Education Technology, Racing and Wagering, and Transportation committees.

priorities.text: On housing: "We need to promote the development of more affordable, equitable, and accessible housing. I will fight to ensure that Harlem families are not priced out of our great village. Moreover, I will work tirelessly to promote ownership opportunities for Harlemites seeking to invest in both residential and commercial real estate."

On jobs and climate: "The development and upgrades needed to address the housing crisis represent a chance for our community to learn skills that not only can lead to careers in labor unions, but also BIPOC-led businesses that hire locally. Climate change is also an emergency that has created a once in a lifetime chance to bring high paying jobs and billions of dollars of economic development to our community."

On youth and education: "We must ensure that youth growing up in Harlem have the necessary infrastructure around them to live up to their full potential. This includes resources devoted to mental health, afterschool programs, academic advisors, workforce opportunities, green spaces, and public safety."

positions.summary: Supports promoting development of more affordable, equitable and accessible housing and expanding home-ownership opportunities for Harlem residents.

record.text: Voted yes on S.10113, allowing a licensed cannabis microbusiness to also serve as a processor and cultivator for cannabis showcase event permits; passed the Assembly 88-53.
Voted yes on S.3460, granting employees access to their personnel records, which passed the Assembly 92-49.

researchNotes: Wright has not completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (his most detailed public statements are from his 2024 survey, cited here) and his official Assembly press page listed no press releases as of research. He has been in office only since January 2025, so his official voting/bill record is thin; only two contested 2026 floor votes were found in the roll-call snapshot this guide draws on. Depth is marked 'basic' accordingly, though he is unopposed for re-election.
